6121.stem:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been produced from Point $O$.

\exfigure{497_q29_1}

figures.cap: compass radial survey of field ABCD from point O

parts.latex: Show that the value of $\angle BOC$ is $105^\circ$.
Find the area of triangle $BOC$ to the nearest square metre.
Show that the value of $\angle AOD$ is $67^\circ$.
Find the perimeter of triangle $AOD$ to the nearest metre.

solutions.latex:
Using the area of a triangle formula with $\angle BOC = 105^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 73 \times 66 \times \sin 105^\circ \\ &\approx 2327 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes into the area formula, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in triangle $AOD$ to find $AD = a$:
$$\begin{aligned} a^2 &= 98^2 + 101^2 - 2 \times 98 \times 101 \cos 67^\circ \\ a &\approx 110 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 110 + 98 + 101 \\ &= 309 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the length $AD$, or equivalent merit
Substitutes into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

497_q29_1.notes: Compass radial survey: the quadrilateral ABCD and radials from O, with lengths written along the lines, bearings beside each vertex and NOT TO SCALE. The dashed N line is drawn exactly vertical from O (draw level, rule 1); the crop leans slightly, which explains the blue/red pair at N. Point names are in maths italic (rule 19) and arrows are filled Latex heads (rule 4).

6206.stem:
Council-member Ashleen would like to establish an annual kayak race on the lake. The course is traced below. The course from the start (point A) to point B is 150m on a true bearing of $054^\circ$. At B the course has a sharp change in direction. The distance from B to C is 170m and $\angle ABC$ is $75^\circ$.

\exfigure{3307_q6_1}

figures.cap: Kayak course triangle ABC on a lake with north arrow
solution sketch: Lake diagram with bearing angles 54°, 36°, 39° annotated in the guidelines

parts.latex: What is the bearing from B to C?
What is the distance from C to A, correct to the nearest m?

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in triangle $ABC$:

$$\begin{aligned} CA^2 &= 150^2 + 170^2 - 2 \times 150 \times 170 \times \cos 75^\circ \\ &\approx 38\,200 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} CA &= \sqrt{38\,200} \\ &\approx 195 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct use of the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

3307_q6_1.notes: Lake outline traced and smoothed, with the island hole, filled in house grey instead of light blue (rule 6). The course triangle is drawn as aux-dashed lines with arrowheads at B, C and A, matching the crop's directions. The North arrow is black. Labels on the shading use \halo (rule 5b). The lower scores come from the scan's thick blue outline and heavy dashes, which are now 0.6pt house dashes.

3307_q6_s1.notes: Same lake as q6_1. The teacher's pink working is redrawn cleanly: a north line at A with the 54° arc between north and AB, and a west line at B with the 36° arc (to BA) and the 39° arc (to BC). The arcs are true circular arcs on the arms, with the values on the bisectors and set in \halo (rules 22, 11, 17). The sketch's geometry is kept as drawn, so it is not to scale (rule 1). Lower scores come from the blue fill and scan strokes, and from the handwritten numbers now being typeset.

figures.cap: lake with Fiona's position and the width of the lake

parts.latex:
Fiona needs to find the width of a lake. From her position she can measure the distance to each side of the lake and the angle between those lines. Which rule would be best for her to use to find the width of the lake?

\exfigure{496_q6_1}

solutions.latex:
Two sides ($a$ and $b$) and the included angle $C$ are known, and the opposite side $c$ is required.

So use the cosine rule:
$$c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$$
So the correct option is A.

496_q6_1.notes: Lake is a smooth irregular outline matching the crop's blob, with the blue fill replaced by the flat house grey (rules 5, 6). Width line, the two sight lines to Fiona, and the Width arrow (filled Latex head, rule 4) all match the crop. 'Width' is written on the grey with \halo (rule 5b). The low original-coverage score is only because the crop's large solid-blue fill counts as ink; every line and label lines up.
